senses.definition: In a sharp manner, in various senses.

subsenses.definition: So as to terminate in a sharp point or edge.
examples: The stick was sharply tapered at one end.
When I touched the snake it recoiled sharply.

quotes.text: The economy has slowed to a pale shadow of its growth in recent years; inflation is high, the currency is declining sharply against the dollar — but the expectations of Brazilians have rarely been higher, feeding broad intolerance with corruption, bad schools and other government failings.
quotes.reference: 2013 June 18, Simon Romero, “Protests Widen as Brazilians Chide Leaders”, in New York Times, retrieved 21 Jun 2013:

subsenses.definition: (to describe breathing) Suddenly and intensely like a gasp, but typically as the result of an emotional reaction.

examples: Jones, the centre forward, started the game sharply.

quotes.text: Walters tried a long range shot in the third minute as he opened the game sharply, linking well with Robbie Keane, but goalkeeper Sergei Pareiko gathered the ball with ease.
quotes.reference: 2011 November 11, Rory Houston, “Estonia 0-4 Republic of Ireland”, in RTE Sport:

subsenses.definition: Of speech, sternly, harshly or critically.
examples: When I asked her about her husband, she replied sharply that she had not seen him for several months.

quotes.text: Before long Tinette stuck her head round the door, and said sharply, 'You're to go to the study.'
quotes.reference: 1956 [1880], Johanna Spyri, Heidi, translation of original by Eileen Hall, page 99:

examples: He was sharply dressed in an expensive suit.

subsenses.definition: So as to form a sharp, or tight, angle.

quotes.text: The last 61 miles of the journey, from Kongsberg to Oslo, are through much less mountainous country. The railway curves sharply away from the Lågan^([sic]), and descends steadily, and in places steeply, past the head of Lake Fiskerumvatn to Hokksund, where the connecting line to the Bergen-Oslo Railway at Hønefoss diverges.
quotes.reference: 1956 April, H. A. Vallance, “To Oslo via Stavanger”, in Railway Magazine, page 219:

examples: His old war wound twinged sharply.

subsenses.definition: In an intellectually alert and penetrating manner.

quotes.text: Peter, after the manner of man at the breakfast table, had allowed half his kedgeree to get cold and was sniggering over a letter. Sophia looked at him sharply. The only letter she had received was from her mother. Sophia's mother was not a humourist.
quotes.reference: 1921, Ben Travers, chapter 1, in A Cuckoo in the Nest, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, Page & Company, published 1925, →OCLC:

subsenses.definition: In a strongly distinguishing or differentiating manner; acutely.
examples: The wealth of this small country contrasts sharply with that of its neighbours.

quotes.text: Hynes is careful to direct the credit to his paymasters in the Scottish Government, whose ambitions for rail contrast increasingly sharply with those in Westminster.
quotes.reference: 2023 November 15, Paul Clifton, “Early responses to Scottish fares trial”, in RAIL, number 996, pages 44-45:
